# FIX-1187 — office-promotion manifest (shape B). THIS FILE IS AN AUTHORISATION.
# The five sitting Senators whose source_ids.fec_candidate_id carries a HOUSE
# CAND_ID. They are the complete class: a prod read on 2026-09-16 of every active
# elected row whose fec_candidate_id prefix disagrees with its role_title returned
# exactly these five, and each has exactly two candidate stubs — one holding the
# House id, one holding the Senate id. The Senate stub holds the live money.
# WHAT A ROW AUTHORISES, in one transaction:
#   1. survivor.source_ids.fec_candidate_id      <- current_id (the SENATE id)
#      survivor.source_ids.prior_fec_candidate_ids += prior_id (the HOUSE id)
#   2. merge senate_stub into survivor as an ordinary pair on current_id
#   3. retire current_id on senate_stub (fec_candidate_id -> merged_fec_candidate_ids)
# house_stub is listed for cross-reference ONLY and is NOT merged by this set. It
# is already an ordinary shape-A pair today, because the survivor's live
# fec_candidate_id IS the House id, so it rides the 151-row shared-id manifest
# (set 1). Keeping the two stubs in separate sets is load-bearing, not tidiness:
# _manifest is (survivor PRIMARY KEY, dup UNIQUE) because the merge SQL assumes
# 1:1, and two stubs for one survivor would move both stubs' colliding rows onto
# the survivor and violate financial_relationships_relcycle_unique. SET 1 MUST RUN
# BEFORE SET 2.
# EVIDENCE. Every Senate id was verified against the OpenFEC API on 2026-09-16
# (https://api.open.fec.gov/v1/candidate/<ID>/). The evidence column carries the
# returned name / state / office_full / party verbatim. A row with an empty
# evidence column is REFUSED by the script — shape B rewrites an identity, not
# just money, so the authorisation has to be per-row and checkable.
# The collision direction is expected to be the OPPOSITE of set 1's here: the
# Senate stub holds the live binding and the survivor's own 2024/2026 rows are
# stale May copies, so the dup should win most ties. cc-129 reports the split
# separately from set 1's rather than folding them together.
